rationale: Vacancies or defects do not invalidate RERA Authority proceedings; unrelated to ratification by a principal.
Agency coupled with an interest cannot be terminated; on agency but not ratification of unauthorised acts.
A person may ratify or disown acts done on his behalf without authority, and ratification has the same effect as prior authority.
Ratification may be express or implied from conduct; a qualification on how ratification happens.
No valid ratification by a person whose knowledge of the facts is materially defective; a condition on ratification.
Ratifying an unauthorised act ratifies the whole transaction it forms part of; a rule on the effect of ratification.
Appointment of pollution analysts under shipping law; 'appointment' in a different sense.
Parties fix the number of arbitrators (odd), failing which a sole arbitrator; needed context but not the appointment procedure.
Section 11 (appointment of arbitrators, including by the court on failure to agree) is the direct answer but is not admitted.
Conciliator not bound by the CPC or Evidence Act; on conciliation but not confidentiality.
Conciliation of sexual harassment complaints under the POSH Act; different Act and says nothing about confidentiality.
The conciliator and parties must keep all matters of the conciliation proceedings, including the settlement agreement, confidential.
The conciliator must not disclose information a party gives on condition of confidentiality; a specific confidentiality rule.
Bars parties from using settlement views, admissions and proposals from conciliation as evidence in other proceedings.
Composition of the State Advisory Board on disability; not job reservation.
Non-discrimination in government employment; related but says nothing about reserved vacancies.
Requires at least four per cent of vacancies in government establishments to be filled by persons with benchmark disabilities, with category split and carry-forward.
Government must identify posts for the reserved vacancies under section 34; the companion procedure.
Access to justice for persons with disabilities; not guardianship.
Reproductive rights; not guardianship.
Children with disabilities not to be separated from parents; not guardianship of persons with disabilities.
Lets a district court or designated authority grant limited guardianship, defines it, deems existing guardians limited guardians and provides an appeal.
Equal legal capacity and rules on support arrangements, the framework within which guardianship operates.
States implement entitlement schemes; on entitlements but not the allowance for non-supply.
Repeal of the ordinance and savings; not the allowance.
Persons not supplied their entitled foodgrains or meals are entitled to a food security allowance from the State Government.
Offence of publishing obscene material electronically; not the power to block access.
Power to authorise monitoring of traffic data for cyber security; a related government power but not blocking.
Offence of publishing sexually explicit material; not blocking.
Offence of cyber terrorism; not the blocking power.
Offence relating to child sexual abuse material; not blocking.
Offence of circumventing technological protection measures; unrelated.
RTI Act exclusion for intelligence organisations; unrelated to website blocking.
RTI rejection on copyright grounds; unrelated.
Empowers the Central Government to direct blocking of public access to information through any computer resource, with penalty for non-complying intermediaries.
Punishment for adulterated products; unrelated to identity theft.
Punishment for spurious goods; unrelated to identity theft.
Penalty for disclosing records accessed under IT Act powers; a related privacy wrong but not misuse of another's password or signature.
Punishes fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's electronic signature, password or unique identification feature.
